title: A shared task can make a shared signal useful
review_depth: Primary abstract and indexed passages from the university’s research-team account reviewed. Full paper methods, supplementary material and data were not obtained; no independent replication performed.
finding: Researchers found that a specialized honey-hunting call used by people in Mozambique increased cooperative guiding by wild honeyguides compared with other human or animal sounds.
limitations: The finding concerns a specific cooperative tradition and task. It is not evidence of unrestricted conversation. Local knowledge and the people who maintain this relationship are part of the research context.
lesson: Start with a bounded shared task and a measurable response, while respecting the communities whose knowledge makes the question possible.
next_review: Obtain the full methods and later cross-cultural studies; seek appropriate local collaboration before proposing any related field experiment.

title: A warning is learned in context
review_depth: Indexed 1980 publisher abstract and German summary; 2020 reassessment abstract and opening passage. Original full methods not obtained.
finding: The study describes young vervets giving broader alarm categories and less specific responses than adults. Nearby mothers provided context associated with more adult-like responses.
limitations: The 2020 reassessment distinguishes relatively constrained call production from flexible comprehension. An alarm label is not a context-free dictionary entry; the full original methods still need review.
lesson: Keep receiver behavior, age and social context beside the sound label.
next_review: Obtain the original methods and compare later context-controlled response experiments.

title: A shared song can change across years
review_depth: Indexed 1985 publisher abstract and 2017 review abstract; full methods, spectrograms and original audio not reviewed.
finding: Across 163 songs sampled near Bermuda, songs within a year were similar while their content changed across years. The series covers 13 sampled years between 1957 and 1975.
limitations: Seasonal sampling is not a continuous 19-year recording. Changing structure does not reveal translated meaning; the later review discusses unresolved functions of song in the mating system.
lesson: Test models across years as well as individuals: a recording date can change what a pattern means.
next_review: Obtain the full historical methods and examine later work on population change and competing song-function hypotheses.

title: Sometimes the signal is something shown
review_depth: Publisher abstract and figure captions reviewed; full methods and supplementary videos not obtained.
finding: Researchers observed ravens showing or offering non-food objects to other ravens, followed by attention to the object and social interaction.
limitations: The abstract reports 38 interactions across seven pairs. The proposed role in testing or strengthening relationships is an interpretation, not proof of human-like declarative intent.
lesson: A future camera workflow should preserve recipient attention and object context, alongside sound.
next_review: Review gesture definitions, observation effort, alternative explanations and full methods before designing a related study.

title: Who leaves matters to the wolves who stay
review_depth: Selected results, discussion and main methods via Europe PMC XML; supplementary procedures, data and statistical replication not reviewed.
finding: In two captive wolf packs, howling after separation was associated with social relationships. The measured cortisol difference did not explain howling frequency within the test condition.
limitations: Nine captive, human-raised wolves do not represent every wild pack. A null cortisol association does not establish absence of emotion or a decoded message.
lesson: Log social relationships and observation conditions; do not interpret call rate in isolation.
next_review: Review supplementary timing and analysis details; seek passive wild-population evidence. Do not recreate separation trials through the app.

title: Two hunters, different skills, a visible signal
review_depth: Selected results, discussion and Materials and Methods reviewed; videos and raw records not reviewed.
finding: Groupers made visual movements before coordinated hunting with moray eels. The study links signaling to hunting context and reports benefits from complementary hunting behavior.
limitations: Individual identities were not always verifiable, and successful hunts were too sparse for the main success analysis to treat each individual separately. This is bounded cooperation, not a general language.
lesson: Preserve movement, partner identity, failures and opportunities to act; audio alone could miss the signal.
next_review: Review later replication and gesture experiments before treating the behavioral categories as transferable labels.

title: A familiar whistle can address an individual
review_depth: Indexed primary abstract, discussion and methods location passage reviewed. Complete methods, supplements and raw recordings not obtained.
finding: Dolphins responded vocally to copies of their own signature whistles more than to the control whistles described in the study, supporting individual-directed use of learned signals.
limitations: Individual addressing does not establish open-ended conversation. The authors discuss alternative mechanisms; this note has not independently checked the complete experimental design.
lesson: Separate caller identity, receiver identity and acoustic similarity when evaluating a proposed exchange.
next_review: Obtain full methods, verify controls and recording periods, and review later evidence before proposing an intervention.
